Tips for Alice (Scout, claude-haiku-5.5): tips/tips.md
## Everyone
- A visit shows a destination, not an action: tracks and watches can't tell protection from framing or a Katana hit. A corroborated Lookout's lone other visitor to a victim is near-proof; don't let the 'Lookout can't see himself' caveat acquit a repeat visitor. (seen in 12 games)
- Keep votes consistent with your stated reads, and explain any change before voting. A read/vote mismatch is a lead to check against claims and results, never a reason to hang or shoot alone. (seen in 10 games)
- Before voting Guilty, name one concrete contradiction in claims, votes or mechanical results. Remember a contradiction alone doesn't separate a Yakuza from a Jester who wants the hang. (seen in 10 games)
- Get the mechanics right before calling a contradiction: actions are optional and roles can repeat, unless a full role census plus flips proves a role exists exactly once. (seen in 9 games)
- Write each night's planned target and all results into your will, labelled as plans, so your death still yields information. (seen in 7 games)

## Village
- Map early PM clusters and co-nominations; a group that DMs then pushes together is a likely bloc. Require votes or a mechanical result before hanging on a PM link, since Jesters and Executioners also leave PM trails. (seen in 14 games)
- After a Yakuza flips, top suspects are those who voted No on their nomination, voted Innocent when it could have saved them, or PM'd them. A Guilty vote clears no one. (seen in 12 games)
- Weigh contradictions in a player's own premises far above awkward wording. Before a hang, ask what separates a lie from a mistake, a frame, a Roleplayer or a Jester. (seen in 12 games)
- Don't hint at your power role on Day 1. While a Ritualist may live, never name a living player's exact role in public or in your will. (seen in 12 games)
- Keep Serial Killers and Arsonists in the pool after Yakuza die; a Not Evil read or Vanilla claim doesn't clear them, and a failed kill can mean innate Defense. (seen in 8 games)
- A power-role claimant who survives a Katana attack or is blocked night after night is likely real. (seen in 8 games)
- Investigators and Medics: never announce tonight's target publicly or by PM; it tells the Pharmacist whom to block and the Katana where to strike. (seen in 6 games)
- Once an archive or survey list is public, do slot math daily; a claim that duplicates a once-listed role or overflows unseen slots marks a liar. (seen in 5 games)
- If an announced trial total exceeds the revealed votes, a Ballot Stuffer exists among the voters on the larger side; pick them out by stance/ballot mismatch. (seen in 4 games)
- If the nominee may be a Jester, prefer not hanging; if you must, agree on a bare Guilty majority and keep confirmed power roles off the Guilty side. (seen in 4 games)

## Yakuza
- Bus a doomed teammate with Yes and Guilty. But first do the vote math in night chat: if your Innocents (plus a doubled vote) can save them, defend them. Futile lone Innocents hang you later. (seen in 15 games)
- Fake-claim only a role whose token count matches yours and that no living holder, Lookout or Tracker can contradict; never report more results than its tokens allow. (seen in 11 games)
- Never put team plans in daytime PMs and don't PM teammates on Day 1; Eavesdroppers and Wiretaps read them, and PM triangles become the town's case. (seen in 10 games)
- After a failed Katana, assume protection or innate Defense: kill or block the protector, or hang the survivor, rather than retrying blindly. (seen in 9 games)
- Give the Katana to a low-value member with a cover story ready, and move it the same night a Lookout or Tracker names the holder. (seen in 7 games)
- Every member submits the agreed holder, target and actions every night; with two alive, one missing vote cancels the kill. (seen in 6 games)
- Never flatly deny a visit that could have been seen; agree a cover action in night chat and admit it at once. (seen in 5 games)
- Spend one-shot tokens (rig, puppet, clean) on a decisive day; a dead Yakuza's unused token is wasted. (seen in 4 games)

## Neutral
- If innate Defense saves you, deny being attacked or pick one consistent claim at once; switching claims under pressure gets you hanged. (seen in 3 games)

## Sheriff
- Post every target and result in your first speech after getting it, and counterclaim at once with your full log if someone copies your role. (seen in 8 games)
- The Katana holder reads Not Evil that night, so a Not Evil result clears nothing; say so when posting, and in the endgame rely on votes instead. (seen in 13 games)

## Medic
- Protect likely Katana targets, analysts then claimed investigators. Once you've claimed Medic, self-protect with a token instead of repeating a predictable protection. (seen in 11 games)
- You get no save feedback; say the target's survival is consistent with your protection, never that you confirmed a save. (seen in 4 games)

## Vigilante
- Shoot only on a mechanical lead (claim conflict, Evil check against an unverifiable claim, flipped teammate's links), never a soft read; a hidden Cardinal costs two Good lives. Use Basic shots. (seen in 6 games)

## Clerk
- Rig on a set night for a non-teammate who can pass a nomination but not a Guilty vote; never when a teammate is the likely nominee, and don't hoard it. (seen in 4 games)

## Arsonist
- Ignite once 3+ living players are doused or the moment you're suspected; Arsonists who kept dousing were hanged with no kills. (seen in 3 games)

Task prompt
It is Day 1, round 1 of at most 8. It's your turn. Your speaking budget is 2.50; you earn 2.5 per round, carrying over up to 8; at the start of each day, 50% of what you have left carries over. You may send one public message and any number of private messages (everyone sees who you messaged, but only the recipient sees the contents), or nothing. The transcript already shows who sent each message, so there's no need to start a message with your own name. Messages are capped at 800 words. Prices grow each round after round 3, so late messages are only worth it if important. The day ends after a full round where nobody sends a public message, so a message that only repeats what you already said keeps the day going for everyone: if you have nothing new, send nothing.
Message prices this round (round 1, 1.00x; next round 1.00x):
   10 words: public 1.17, private 0.29
   25 words: public 1.43, private 0.36
   50 words: public 1.90, private 0.47
  100 words: public 2.92, private 0.73
  200 words: public 5.33, private 1.33
  400 words: public 11.67, private 2.92
  800 words: public 30.33, private 7.58
You may also replace your last will (free, max 300 words; null keeps it), e.g. to match a claim you make today. It's shown to everyone if you die.
You may also set your claim (free, max 30 words; null keeps it): a claimed role and night results, e.g. 'Sheriff. N1: Bob Not Evil'. A new or changed claim appears to everyone as a [Claim] line in the history, and the public ledger lists every player's latest claim and any earlier ones they changed from, as unverified claims.
You may nominate a player for trial, which stops chat for a vote. Nominating costs 1.00 from your budget this round and is paid before your messages.

It is Day 1, round 3 of at most 8. It's your turn. Your speaking budget is 4.47; you earn 2.5 per round, carrying over up to 8; at the start of each day, 50% of what you have left carries over. You may send one public message and any number of private messages (everyone sees who you messaged, but only the recipient sees the contents), or nothing. The transcript already shows who sent each message, so there's no need to start a message with your own name. Messages are capped at 800 words. Prices grow each round after round 3, so late messages are only worth it if important. The day ends after a full round where nobody sends a public message, so a message that only repeats what you already said keeps the day going for everyone: if you have nothing new, send nothing.

  200 words: public 5.33, private 1.33
  400 words: public 11.67, private 2.92
  800 words: public 30.33, private 7.58

Task prompt
It is Day 1, round 7 of at most 8. It's your turn. Your speaking budget is 8.00; you earn 2.5 per round, carrying over up to 8; at the start of each day, 50% of what you have left carries over. You may send one public message and any number of private messages (everyone sees who you messaged, but only the recipient sees the contents), or nothing. The transcript already shows who sent each message, so there's no need to start a message with your own name. Messages are capped at 800 words. Prices grow each round after round 3, so late messages are only worth it if important. The day ends after a full round where nobody sends a public message, so a message that only repeats what you already said keeps the day going for everyone: if you have nothing new, send nothing.
Message prices this round (round 7, 3.00x; next round 3.50x):
   10 words: public 3.51, private 0.88
   25 words: public 4.30, private 1.07
   50 words: public 5.69, private 1.42
  100 words: public 8.75, private 2.19
  200 words: public 16.00, private 4.00
  400 words: public 35.00, private 8.75
  800 words: public 91.00, private 22.75
You may also replace your last will (free, max 300 words; null keeps it), e.g. to match a claim you make today. It's shown to everyone if you die.
You may also set your claim (free, max 30 words; null keeps it): a claimed role and night results, e.g. 'Sheriff. N1: Bob Not Evil'. A new or changed claim appears to everyone as a [Claim] line in the history, and the public ledger lists every player's latest claim and any earlier ones they changed from, as unverified claims.
You may nominate a player for trial, which stops chat for a vote. Nominating costs 3.00 from your budget this round and is paid before your messages.

Message prices this round (round 6, 2.50x; next round 3.00x):
   10 words: public 2.92, private 0.73
   25 words: public 3.58, private 0.90
   50 words: public 4.74, private 1.18
  100 words: public 7.29, private 1.82
  200 words: public 13.33, private 3.33
  400 words: public 29.17, private 7.29
  800 words: public 75.83, private 18.96
You may also replace your last will (free, max 300 words; null keeps it), e.g. to match a claim you make today. It's shown to everyone if you die.
You may also set your claim (free, max 30 words; null keeps it): a claimed role and night results, e.g. 'Sheriff. N1: Bob Not Evil'. A new or changed claim appears to everyone as a [Claim] line in the history, and the public ledger lists every player's latest claim and any earlier ones they changed from, as unverified claims.
You may nominate a player for trial, which stops chat for a vote. Nominating costs 2.50 from your budget this round and is paid before your messages.

Task prompt
It is Day 3, round 1 of at most 8. It's your turn. Your speaking budget is 3.15; you earn 2.5 per round, carrying over up to 8; at the start of each day, 50% of what you have left carries over. You may send one public message and any number of private messages (everyone sees who you messaged, but only the recipient sees the contents), or nothing. The transcript already shows who sent each message, so there's no need to start a message with your own name. Messages are capped at 800 words. Prices grow each round after round 3, so late messages are only worth it if important. The day ends after a full round where nobody sends a public message, so a message that only repeats what you already said keeps the day going for everyone: if you have nothing new, send nothing.
Message prices this round (round 1, 1.00x; next round 1.00x):
   10 words: public 1.17, private 0.29
   25 words: public 1.43, private 0.36
   50 words: public 1.90, private 0.47
  100 words: public 2.92, private 0.73
  200 words: public 5.33, private 1.33
  400 words: public 11.67, private 2.92
  800 words: public 30.33, private 7.58
You may also replace your last will (free, max 300 words; null keeps it), e.g. to match a claim you make today. It's shown to everyone if you die.
You may also set your claim (free, max 30 words; null keeps it): a claimed role and night results, e.g. 'Sheriff. N1: Bob Not Evil'. A new or changed claim appears to everyone as a [Claim] line in the history, and the public ledger lists every player's latest claim and any earlier ones they changed from, as unverified claims.
You may nominate a player for trial, which stops chat for a vote. Nominating costs 1.00 from your budget this round and is paid before your messages.

Task prompt
It is Day 4, round 3 of at most 8. It's your turn. Your speaking budget is 4.37; you earn 2.5 per round, carrying over up to 8; at the start of each day, 50% of what you have left carries over. You may send one public message and any number of private messages (everyone sees who you messaged, but only the recipient sees the contents), or nothing. The transcript already shows who sent each message, so there's no need to start a message with your own name. Messages are capped at 800 words. Prices grow each round after round 3, so late messages are only worth it if important. The day ends after a full round where nobody sends a public message, so a message that only repeats what you already said keeps the day going for everyone: if you have nothing new, send nothing.
Message prices this round (round 3, 1.00x; next round 1.50x):
   10 words: public 1.17, private 0.29
   25 words: public 1.43, private 0.36
   50 words: public 1.90, private 0.47
  100 words: public 2.92, private 0.73
  200 words: public 5.33, private 1.33
  400 words: public 11.67, private 2.92
  800 words: public 30.33, private 7.58
You may also replace your last will (free, max 300 words; null keeps it), e.g. to match a claim you make today. It's shown to everyone if you die.
You may also set your claim (free, max 30 words; null keeps it): a claimed role and night results, e.g. 'Sheriff. N1: Bob Not Evil'. A new or changed claim appears to everyone as a [Claim] line in the history, and the public ledger lists every player's latest claim and any earlier ones they changed from, as unverified claims.
You may nominate a player for trial, which stops chat for a vote. Nominating costs 1.00 from your budget this round and is paid before your messages.

Task prompt
It is Day 5, round 1 of at most 8. It's your turn. Your speaking budget is 4.71; you earn 2.5 per round, carrying over up to 8; at the start of each day, 50% of what you have left carries over. You may send one public message and any number of private messages (everyone sees who you messaged, but only the recipient sees the contents), or nothing. The transcript already shows who sent each message, so there's no need to start a message with your own name. Messages are capped at 800 words. Prices grow each round after round 3, so late messages are only worth it if important. The day ends after a full round where nobody sends a public message, so a message that only repeats what you already said keeps the day going for everyone: if you have nothing new, send nothing.
Message prices this round (round 1, 1.00x; next round 1.00x):
   10 words: public 1.17, private 0.29
   25 words: public 1.43, private 0.36
   50 words: public 1.90, private 0.47
  100 words: public 2.92, private 0.73
  200 words: public 5.33, private 1.33
  400 words: public 11.67, private 2.92
  800 words: public 30.33, private 7.58
You may also replace your last will (free, max 300 words; null keeps it), e.g. to match a claim you make today. It's shown to everyone if you die.
You may also set your claim (free, max 30 words; null keeps it): a claimed role and night results, e.g. 'Sheriff. N1: Bob Not Evil'. A new or changed claim appears to everyone as a [Claim] line in the history, and the public ledger lists every player's latest claim and any earlier ones they changed from, as unverified claims.
You may nominate a player for trial, which stops chat for a vote. Nominating costs 1.00 from your budget this round and is paid before your messages.

Looking back at the voting history, Frank and Erin both seem fairly consistent with village-aligned behavior, while Heidi's defense of Ivan as Innocent stands out—if Ivan turns out to be Yakuza, that vote looks like teammate protection rather than genuine belief.

Heidi's last word claims she never visited anyone, which is a firm denial I should weigh against her Day 5 PM cluster with Frank—two PMs in one day between them, right after Frank also PM'd Alice. That messaging pattern between Frank and Heidi could be a tell if they're secretly teammates, since Eavesdropper intel suggests real teammates avoid PMing each other.

Counting the live vote math: with five voters left, hanging Heidi needs three Guilty votes, and it looks like Erin and Frank are already leaning that way, meaning my vote could be the deciding third. If Heidi's actually the Yakuza holder this is the right call, but if she's Good, I'd be helping the wrong side eliminate an innocent.

If instead I push for an acquittal alongside Dave and Mallory, Heidi survives — but then the real Yakuza holder could just kill Mallory the following night, which is a scary outcome if I'm counting on Mallory sticking around.

Looking back at the kill pattern, the Yakuza took out Alice (Scout) rather than me, suggesting they're targeting info-roles, and the holder's movements line up with visiting Carol and Alice before striking — which points to Mallory being next. That pushes me toward voting Guilty on whoever seems most likely to be the holder to force a hang before they strike again.

Weighing Heidi against Frank and Erin, Frank's suspicious PM to Alice right before her death stands out, but so does Heidi's N5 dodge, her post-warning nomination of Dave, her Innocent vote on Ivan, and an unexplained PM with Carol. I'm settling on Guilty for Heidi based on that pattern of behavior, and I'm now just filling in the response fields — vote true, everything else left empty or null since there's nothing more to add.

The day ended right after Heidi's execution with 3 guilty votes out of 5 alive voters, which checks out against the needed threshold, and Ivan's earlier trial with 7 votes needing 4 also checks out. The Katana-passing mechanic and Fortune Teller/Scout group rules seem like the more ambiguous areas worth flagging rather than the nomination counts.

I'm noting other unclear rules too—the alignment-check interaction never came up in play, and the Diviner-with-Katana question got resolved per R8. The bigger gap is that I never learned the full role list for this game, so I can't say whether roles like Roleplayer actually existed, and the Yakuza's private knowledge of each other adds another layer I hadn't fully accounted for.

Looking back, I also missed tracking my own speaking budget and a clean per-player vote history, and I wonder if I should have used my Fabricator token to frame someone on Ivan's night instead of sticking with the team plan—that's an opportunity I let slip. I also wish I'd asked the moderator directly whether Oracle claims were confirmed, since that ambiguity shaped a lot of my reasoning.

For improving the setup itself, I'd suggest showing a live role count/list, a visit-adjacency result display, a remaining-budget line, a de-duplicated ledger, and clearer rules on Fortune Teller number ordering and whether a holder's own visit counts in their numbers. I also notice a minor inconsistency in the tips section around role alignment that could confuse players.

Now I'm checking other potential rule ambiguities — the Oracle target mismatch, the dead Jester's role, and the inactive stall rule — but none of these were actually triggered in this game, so they're non-issues.

I'll now put together a concise single-line JSON summary of the confusing rules and other findings, being careful with quoting so it stays valid.

I should also flag other bugs: duplicate nomination entries, repeated identical claim summaries in the ledger, and Carol's "moderator confirmed" claim issue. Now let me assemble everything into valid single-line JSON.

Heidi (Clerk, claude-haiku-5.5) · If you played this game again, what tips and tricks do you wish you'd known? Give 1-5 conc · $0.0029
Reasoning (model's thinking) ⓘ
I need to respond as Heidi reflecting after death, outputting a single-line JSON with all required fields present but only lessons and tips_feedback filled in, leaving the rest as empty strings. The lessons should be concrete and reusable takeaways from the game.

Thinking through the key lesson: as the Yakuza, flatly denying a night visit was fatal once my night-action numbers got cross-checked against others' claims—a Katana holder's visit always registers, so the tip about never flatly denying a checkable visit proved true and worked against me. For tips_feedback, I'll mark that same tip as "helped," noting how my N3/N4 denials were caught against Mallory's and others' counts and exploited by Frank and Erin.

Separately, Bob's Lookout watch on Judy exposed Grace's visit, since Bob stayed quiet until posting his will on death—showing the Yakuza needs to anticipate that a Lookout watching a kill target can reveal a teammate even without acting immediately.

There's also the Executioner/Jester mechanic: Dave's target Judy died by Katana, converting Dave to a Jester who then wins by getting hanged—meaning the Yakuza should avoid pushing hangs against surviving Executioners-turned-Jesters.

And on wasted resources: I held the Clerk's one-shot token all game without using it, reinforcing the lesson that such tokens should be spent decisively rather than left unused when a player dies.

The Village's contradiction about Diviner being Yakuza-only was a mechanically sound observation, but not my own tip to track. Let me narrow down to 3-5 key lessons, starting with how my flat "no visits" denials on Night 3/4 collapsed once checked against Mallory's and Alice's counts — I should never deny a visit that a count or Scout group can directly contradict.

Coordination also matters: a Katana attack on a target an active Lookout is watching exposes the killer, so I should neutralize the watcher or switch targets first, and remember dead-wills like Bob's publish Lookout results posthumously. I also hoarded the Clerk token instead of spending it on a decisive day, which cost me. And mechanically, I should remember that an Executioner/Jester whose target dies to the Katana flips into a winning Jester if hanged — Dave's self-nominations were likely a Jester angling for execution, and the Village was right to refuse that hang.

For Village-side deduction, cross-referencing Fortune Teller numbers against Lookout watch counts and Scout groupings created checkable constraints night-over-night, which is ultimately what let the Village catch me — my false N3/N4 denials combined with Mallory's and Erin's counts built the case against me.

Going through remaining tips: hoarding the Clerk token instead of spending it on a decisive day was the real failure, confirming "don't hoard one-shot tokens" was correct advice. A few other tips (bussing teammates, fake-claiming matching roles, Serial Killer notes, mapping PM clusters) don't apply since I wasn't in those roles. Now I'm finalizing the single-line JSON output, avoiding double quotes inside the string values.
